nodes.body: `compile` takes `_input` only to satisfy the seam signature, but it’s currently unused. If `no-unused-vars` is enabled (or enabled later), this will start failing lint; also, explicitly consuming the arg makes the intent clearer.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Return cloned compiled prompt fixtures**

When the sample mock is used more than once, `compile()` now returns the same module-level `compiledPromptFixture` object every time, so any caller that mutates the returned prompt or nested `metadata.enforcedConstraints` will corrupt subsequent mock calls and tests. This is a regression from the previous implementation, which built a fresh object per compile, and it is especially easy to hit in downstream seam tests that tweak compiled prompts before passing them to safety/gallery validation; clone the fixture before returning it, as the gallery mock now does for stored records.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Keep the unsafe `CompiledPrompt` cast out of the exported `getCompiledPromptFixture` helper.**  
In `src/lib/seams/prompt-compiler-seam/fixtures.ts` (lines 94-96), the `'fault'` branch returns `compiledPromptFaultFixture as CompiledPrompt` even though the fault fixture is intentionally invalid (e.g., empty `imagePrompt`/`negativePrompt`). This weakens type safety for every caller. Move the fault-only cast into `mock.ts` (or a clearly named fault-only unsafe helper) so only the mock/test layer performs the unsafe conversion.

<details><summary>Current snippet</summary>

```ts
// Cast is intentional: fault path contains an invalid object used for mock fault scenarios.
export const getCompiledPromptFixture = (scenario: 'sample' | 'fault' = 'sample'): CompiledPrompt =>
  scenario === 'fault' ? (compiledPromptFaultFixture as CompiledPrompt) : compiledPromptFixture;
```

</details>
